newsitem.title: ITALY: No change on Albania stance - Italy's Berlusconi.
newsitem.headline: No change on Albania stance - Italy's Berlusconi.

text.p: Italian opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said on Tuesday after a meeting of parties in his centre-right Freedom Alliance that it had not altered its stance on a forthcoming security mission for Albania.
"We are sticking to the position we expressed this morning that the government should vote for our motion," Berlusconi told reporters at the Senate (upper house).
"I don't understand why the government cannot vote for our resolution and thus resolve this practical problem," he said.
The Senate is due to vote later on Tuesday on a mission which has thrown Prime Minister Romano Prodi's majority into disarray and raised questions about his long-term survival.
The session was earlier suspended pending a meeting of parliamentary party leaders on the procedure for the vote.
Prodi is not expected to encounter serious difficulty in the Senate (upper house) vote, where he has a majority.

But the refusal of the Communist Refoundation party to back the government in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house), where it relies on hard-left support, could leave Prodi no option but to vote for an opposition motion to ensure the force goes ahead.
The Chamber is due to vote on the mission on Wednesday.
